public_rationale: Meta was still publicly pursuing the metaverse in March 2023. Its executive held a briefing inside Horizon Workrooms and reaffirmed a long-term commitment. That contradicts having given up on the idea. Greater emphasis on AI does not establish abandonment.
limitations: The decisive item is contemporary Bloomberg reporting rather than a primary transcript.
This assesses abandonment, not whether enthusiasm, publicity, or relative priority declined.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Zuckerberg gave up on the metaverse as soon as AI became the new hype trend.

statement.excerpt: He has spent hours of interviews vaguely mumbling about how the metaverse would change everything, only to give up on the idea the second that artificial intelligence became the new big thing.

from_speaker: the second that artificial intelligence became the new big thing
our_interpretation: The checkable core is that Meta had abandoned pursuing the metaverse, not merely reduced its prominence in communications.
Treat 'the second' as rhetorical immediacy, not a literal timestamp.
For the ongoing strategic state, use March 2023, the latest complete month before the post. Strategy can be publicly reported without waiting for quarterly financial statements.
The descriptions of interview style and duration are background rhetoric, not the core abandonment claim.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporary records show that Meta ceased pursuing the metaverse as a substantive strategy during the period of increased AI emphasis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporary records establish continuing substantive metaverse commitments or activity during that period.
